To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the immobile pupal stage is a vulnerable stage in the life cycle of insects, (2) pupae use a wide range of different antipredator behaviours, (3) the antipredator strategy used by a pupa is often related to the pupal habitat and (4) pupae are rarely aposematic.

pupal predators are common, that pupae are not defenceless, that the most common strategy is to avoid predators, that pupae have also evolved a variety of behavioural and secondary defensives and that the pupal stage is an interesting stage to study the ontogeny of antipredation strategies.

1) the immobile pupae have evolved a wide range of anti-predator strategies against invertebrate as well as vertebrate predators, 2) most of these strategies aim at avoiding encounters with predators and 3) pupae have evolved behavioural and secondary defenses, but not warning coloration, even though pupae often contain defensive chemicals.
